sections.title: Water Image of Clocks (18:30 / 17:90 Rule)
sections.content:
For water image clock problems, use the 18:30 subtraction rule.

Rule: Water Time = 18:30 − Given Time
If minutes are more than 30, you may convert 18:30 into 17:90 for easier subtraction.

Example: 8:20
Step 1: Write 18:30 − 8:20.
Step 2: Subtract minutes and hours carefully.
Step 3: 18:30 − 8:20 = 10:10.
Step 4: Final water image time is 10:10.

sections.title: Mirror Image with Hours, Minutes and Seconds
sections.content:
When seconds are included, apply the 11:60:60 rule.

Rule: Mirror Time = 11:60:60 − Given Time

Example: 10:15:30
Step 1: Write 11:60:60 − 10:15:30.
Step 2: Subtract seconds: 60 − 30 = 30.
Step 3: Subtract minutes: 60 − 15 = 45.
Step 4: Subtract hours: 11 − 10 = 1.
Step 5: Final mirror time is 1:45:30.

sections.title: Mixed Alphanumeric Strings (Mirror Logic)
sections.content:
In mirror image, the entire string is reversed from left to right. Some letters and numbers may also visually change.

Example: B5G7K9
Step 1: Reverse the order → 9K7G5B.
Step 2: Check if any number looks different in mirror (like 2, 3, 5 in some fonts).
Step 3: Adjust visually if required.
Step 4: Match with correct option.

sections.title: Mixed Alphanumeric Strings (Water Logic)
sections.content:
In water image, the order remains the same, but the figure flips upside down.

Example: SSC2024
Step 1: Keep the order same → SSC2024.
Step 2: Imagine each character upside down.
Step 3: Check which characters remain unchanged (0, 8 etc.).
Step 4: Choose the correct visual match.

sections.title: Finding Identical Words in Mirror Image
sections.content:
A word will look identical in mirror only if:
1. The word reads the same after reversal.
2. All letters are vertically symmetrical.

Example: MOM
Step 1: Reverse → MOM.
Step 2: Check symmetry of M and O.
Step 3: Since both are symmetrical, it remains same.
Step 4: MOM is correct.

sections.title: Finding Identical Words in Water Image
sections.content:
For water image identical words:
1. Order remains same.
2. All letters must have horizontal symmetry.

Example: HIDE
Step 1: Keep order same.
Step 2: Check each letter for horizontal symmetry.
Step 3: Letters like H, I, O, X remain same.
Step 4: Select the word where all letters satisfy this condition.

sections.title: Common Level 2 Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Mixing up 11:60 and 18:30 rules.
2. Forgetting to subtract seconds first.
3. Reversing order in water image.
4. Ignoring letter symmetry while choosing identical words.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content:
Mirror Image: Reverse order and apply 11:60 (or 11:60:60).
Water Image: Keep order same and apply 18:30 rule for clocks.
For words and codes, check both order and symmetry carefully.

tricks.title: 18:30 Water Clock Trick
tricks.explanation: Always subtract the given time from 18:30 for water image.

tricks.title: 17:90 Adjustment Trick
tricks.explanation: If minutes are difficult to subtract, convert 18:30 into 17:90.

tricks.title: 11:60:60 Seconds Trick
tricks.explanation: For mirror time with seconds, subtract from 11:60:60.

tricks.title: Reverse First Method
tricks.explanation: In mirror image codes, first reverse the full string.

tricks.title: Water Keeps Order Trick
tricks.explanation: In water image, never reverse the order.

tricks.title: Vertical Symmetry Rule
tricks.explanation: Mirror identical letters: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y.

tricks.title: Horizontal Symmetry Rule
tricks.explanation: Water identical letters: B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X.
tricks.example: BOX works if all letters qualify.

tricks.title: Borrow Carefully Trick
tricks.explanation: While subtracting time, always subtract seconds first and borrow properly.

tricks.title: Elimination Strategy
tricks.explanation: Eliminate options that break order or symmetry rule.
tricks.example: If mirror question, remove same-order options immediately.
